title: Algebraic Expressions: Simplifying, Expanding and Factorising
summary: What letters mean in expressions, formulae and equations; simplifying with the laws of arithmetic (including squares and cubes); expanding a single bracket and factorising by taking out the highest common factor.

blocks.title: In the curriculum
items: Understand that a letter can mean different things: in an **expression** it can stand for any number, in a **formula** it stands for a quantity linked to other quantities, and in an **equation** it stands for an unknown number you can find (8Ae.01)
Use the laws of arithmetic and the order of operations with algebra — adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing terms, including squares and cubes (8Ae.02)
Expand a bracket multiplied by a single term (including answers with squares and cubes), and factorise an expression by taking out the highest common factor (8Ae.03)

blocks.text: Algebra is arithmetic with letters. Every rule you use with numbers — brackets first, multiplication before addition, a × b = b × a — works in exactly the same way with letters. This page teaches you to read algebra correctly, simplify it, multiply out brackets (**expand**) and put brackets back in (**factorise**).
Key words

items: term
حد — a number, a letter, or numbers and letters multiplied together, e.g. 5, x, 3ab, 4y²
coefficient
معامل — the number in front of the letter; in 7x² the coefficient is 7
like terms
حدود متشابهة — terms with exactly the same letters and powers, e.g. 3x and −5x; 2a² and a²
expression
مقدار جبري — terms joined by + or −, with no equals sign, e.g. 3n + 5
formula
قانون / صيغة — a rule linking quantities, e.g. A = lw
equation
معادلة — two sides that are equal, with an unknown to find, e.g. 3n + 5 = 20
variable / unknown
متغير / مجهول — a letter that can change / a letter with a particular value to find
simplify
يبسّط — write in the shortest form by collecting like terms
expand
يفك الأقواس — multiply out the brackets
factorise
يحلل — write as a product by taking out a common factor
highest common factor (HCF)
العامل المشترك الأكبر — the biggest factor shared by all the terms

blocks.text: 1. Expressions, formulae and equations

rows: n can be **any** number (a variable). Different n gives a different value.
Each letter is a **quantity** (area, length, width). Change l or w and A changes.
Equals sign; letters on both sides stand for named quantities; one letter is the subject
n is an **unknown** with a particular value. Here n = 5 only.
Equals sign; you can solve it to find the letter

blocks.text: The same letter can play different roles. In the expression 2t + 1, t can be anything. In the formula s = d/t, t means 'time taken'. In the equation 2t + 1 = 9, t must be 4. Checkpoint may ask you to sort examples into expression / formula / equation, or to say what a letter represents.
2. Writing algebra the standard way

rows: division is written as a fraction

blocks.text: **Order of operations still applies.** 3x² means 3 × x², so square x first, then multiply by 3. (3x)² means work out 3x first, then square. If x = −2: 3x² = 3 × (−2)² = 3 × 4 = **12**, but (3x)² = (−6)² = **36**. And x³ + 4 = (−2)³ + 4 = −8 + 4 = **−4**.

**The laws of arithmetic work with letters:** a + b = b + a and ab = ba (commutative); (a + b) + c = a + (b + c) and (ab)c = a(bc) (associative); a(b + c) = ab + ac (distributive). These laws are why we can collect like terms and expand brackets.
3. Collecting like terms
You can only add or subtract **like terms**: same letters, same powers. Each term owns the sign in front of it. Underline or colour each group of like terms.

rows: ab and ba are like terms

blocks.text: x² and x are **not** like terms (x² = x × x is a different thing from x), so x² + x stays as it is. Also x + x = 2x, but x × x = x².
4. Multiplying and dividing terms
**Multiply the numbers, then multiply the letters.** Same letters multiplied make a power: x × x = x², x × x² = x³. **Divide** by writing it as a fraction and cancelling numbers and letters.
5. Expanding brackets
To **expand** a(b + c), multiply **every** term inside the bracket by the term outside: a(b + c) = ab + ac. An area diagram shows why.

blocks.text: **Expand and simplify:** expand each bracket, then collect like terms. 3(x + 2) + 2(x − 5) = 3x + 6 + 2x − 10 = **5x − 4**. Watch the sign when a negative number is outside the bracket: 5(y + 1) − 2(y − 3) = 5y + 5 − 2y + 6 = **3y + 11**.

blocks.title: فك الأقواس
blocks.text: اضرب الحد اللي برّه القوس في كل حد جوه القوس — كلهم، مش الأول بس. وخلي بالك من الإشارة: سالب × سالب = موجب، يعني −2(x − 4) = −2x + 8. وتذكّر: x × x = x² و x × x² = x³.
6. Factorising (taking out the HCF)
**Factorising** is the reverse of expanding: you put the brackets back in.

blocks.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 95" width="480" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14"><text x="70" y="45" text-anchor="middle" fill="#0f1b33" font-size="20" font-weight="bold">6x² + 9x</text><text x="400" y="45" text-anchor="middle" fill="#1b6e2e" font-size="20" font-weight="bold">3x(2x + 3)</text><line x1="140" y1="30" x2="330" y2="30" stroke="#1b6e2e" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="330.0,30.0 320.8,33.9 320.8,26.1" fill="#1b6e2e"/><text x="235" y="20" text-anchor="middle" fill="#1b6e2e" font-size="13">factorise (take out HCF 3x)</text><line x1="330" y1="62" x2="140" y2="62" stroke="#1f5fbf" stroke-width="2"/><polygon points="140.0,62.0 149.2,58.1 149.2,65.9" fill="#1f5fbf"/><text x="235" y="82" text-anchor="middle" fill="#1f5fbf" font-size="13">expand (multiply out)</text></svg>
blocks.caption: Expanding and factorising are inverse processes.

items: Find the HCF of the **numbers** (coefficients).
Find the HCF of the **letters**: a letter is in the HCF only if it is in every term; use its lowest power.
Write the HCF outside the bracket. Inside, write what each term must be multiplied by to give the original term (divide each term by the HCF).
Check by expanding. 'Factorise **fully**' means you must take out the **highest** common factor.

blocks.text: 8a² − 12a = 2a(4a − 6) is factorised, but **not fully**: 4a − 6 still has a common factor 2. The full answer is 4a(2a − 3).
Worked examples
**Worked example 1** — Write E (expression), F (formula) or Q (equation) for each.  (a) 5y − 2   (b) 5y − 2 = 18   (c) P = 4s, where P is the perimeter of a square of side s.  [2]

items: (a) **Expression** — no equals sign; y can be any number.
(b) **Equation** — it can be solved: 5y = 20, so y = 4.
(c) **Formula** — it links two quantities (perimeter and side length); P changes when s changes.

blocks.text: **Worked example 2** — Simplify  (a) 7m + 3n − 2m − 5n   (b) 4x² + 3x − x² − 7x  [2]

items: (a) m terms: 7m − 2m = 5m. n terms: 3n − 5n = −2n. Answer **5m − 2n**.
(b) x² terms: 4x² − x² = 3x². x terms: 3x − 7x = −4x. Answer **3x² − 4x**.

blocks.text: Common mistake: combining x² and x terms (e.g. writing −x³ or −x² as the answer to (b)). They are not like terms.
**Worked example 3** — Simplify  (a) 5a × 3a   (b) 2b × 3b²   (c) 20c³ ÷ 4c  [3]
**Worked example 4** — x = −3. Work out the value of  (a) 2x²   (b) (2x)²   (c) x³ + 10  [3]

items: (a) Indices before multiplication: x² = (−3)² = 9, then 2 × 9 = **18**.
(b) Brackets first: 2x = −6, then (−6)² = **36**.

blocks.text: Common mistake: in (a) working out (2 × −3)² = 36. Only x is squared in 2x².
**Worked example 5** — Expand and simplify 3(2y + 5) − 2(y − 4).  [2]

items: First bracket: 3 × 2y = 6y, 3 × 5 = 15 → 6y + 15.
Second bracket (the −2 goes with it): −2 × y = −2y, −2 × (−4) = +8 → −2y + 8.

blocks.text: Common mistake: writing −2(y − 4) = −2y − 8. A negative times a negative is positive.
**Worked example 6** — (a) Expand a(a² + 3a).  (b) Factorise fully 12x² − 18x.  [3]

items: (a) a × a² = a³ and a × 3a = 3a² → **a³ + 3a²**.
(b) HCF of 12 and 18 is 6. Both terms contain x; the lowest power is x. HCF = 6x.

blocks.text: **Worked example 7** — Kamal factorises 15n² + 10n and writes 5(3n² + 2n). Is his answer fully factorised? Explain.  [1]

items: **No.** 3n² and 2n still have a common factor of n, so the HCF of the original terms is 5n, not 5.
Fully factorised: **5n(3n + 2)**.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
items: Adding unlike terms: 3x + 2y ≠ 5xy and x² + x ≠ x³.
Mixing up 2x (= x + x) and x² (= x × x).
Multiplying only the first term when expanding: 4(2x − 3) is 8x − 12, not 8x − 3.
Losing the sign: −2(y − 4) = −2y + 8.
Squaring the coefficient by mistake: 3x² with x = 4 is 3 × 16 = 48, not 12² = 144.
Not factorising fully: 8a² − 12a = 4a(2a − 3), not 2(4a² − 6a).
Forgetting the 1 when a whole term is the HCF: 7m + 7 = 7(m + 1), not 7m.

blocks.title: How Checkpoint asks this
items: 'Simplify', 'Expand', 'Expand and simplify', 'Factorise fully' — each has a different meaning; do exactly what the command word says.
'Draw a line from each item to expression, formula or equation' or 'Tick the correct box'.
'Find the value of … when x = −3' — substitute with brackets around negative numbers, and follow the order of operations.
Area of a rectangle with sides like 2x and (x + 5): 'Write an expression for the area. Expand the brackets.'
'Ali says… Is he correct?' — check by expanding or substituting a number. Substituting a number (e.g. x = 2) into both forms is a quick way to test whether two expressions are equal.
Your final answer should be fully simplified; an unsimplified correct expression may lose the last mark.

blocks.text: Practice

blocks.title: Algebraic expressions — practice quiz
blocks.intro: No calculator. Type powers with ^ (x^2, y^3) or use ² ³. Spaces do not matter.

questions.q: Which of these is an equation?
c: V = l × w × h, the volume of a cuboid
questions.e: 3t − 7 and t² + 3t have no equals sign — they are expressions. V = l × w × h links quantities (volume, length, width, height) — it is a formula. 3t − 7 = 11 can be solved (t = 6), so it is an equation.
x² terms: 3x² − x² = 2x². x terms: 5x − 2x = 3x. Answer 2x² + 3x.
Numbers: 4 × 3 = 12. Letters: y × y = y². Answer 12y².
18 ÷ 6 = 3. a³ ÷ a = (a × a × a) ÷ a = a². Answer 3a².

questions.q: (c) Work out the value of x³ − 3x

questions.e: x × x = x² and x × (−6) = −6x. Answer x² − 6x.
HCF of 14 and 21 is 7 (n is not in both terms). 14n ÷ 7 = 2n, 21 ÷ 7 = 3 → 7(2n − 3).
HCF of 9 and 12 is 3; both terms contain x → HCF = 3x. 9x² ÷ 3x = 3x, 12x ÷ 3x = 4 → 3x(3x + 4). Check: 9x² + 12x ✓

questions.q:
Rania says that 6t² + 8t = 2(3t² + 4t) is factorised fully.
Is she correct? Explain your answer and give the fully factorised form.
questions.ms: 1 mark: No, with a reason, e.g. 3t² and 4t still have a common factor of t / the HCF is 2t not 2. 1 mark: 2t(3t + 4) cao. Do not accept 'No' with no reason for the first mark.
questions.e: No. The terms 3t² and 4t inside the bracket still share a factor t, so 2 is not the highest common factor. The HCF of 6t² and 8t is 2t: 6t² ÷ 2t = 3t, 8t ÷ 2t = 4 → 2t(3t + 4).

blocks.title: Remember
items: Expression: no equals sign, letter = any number. Formula: links quantities. Equation: letter = unknown to find.
Only like terms (same letters, same powers) can be added or subtracted.
Multiply terms: numbers × numbers, letters × letters (x × x = x², x × x² = x³). Divide by cancelling.
Expand: multiply every term inside the bracket by the term outside — watch the signs.
Factorise fully: take out the HCF of the numbers AND the letters; check by expanding.
